# Read linked pages with `web_crawl`

`web_crawl` gives an agent content from multiple linked pages on a website.

## When to use it

Use it to read a documentation section, research a company website, or gather context from several related pages. Each successfully extracted page costs one search credit, including the starting page. Set a page limit in application code when registering the tool.

Choose [`web_fetch`](web_fetch.html) for one known page. Pair [`web_map`](web_map.html) with `web_fetch` when the agent should inspect the available URLs before deciding which pages to read.

## Quick example

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_crawl

agent_tools = [
    web_crawl(default_params={"max_pages": 3, "max_depth": 1}),
]
```

With one supported SDK installed, the tool is native to that SDK. Add it to your agent's tool collection. See [Agent SDKs](frameworks.html) for setup and explicit provider selection when multiple SDKs are installed.

An agent can start the crawl with:

```json
{"url": "https://www.python.org/about/"}
```

This configuration reads up to three pages, including the starting page, and follows links at most one level deep. The limits apply to each tool call.

## Inputs the agent can provide

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | The absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the starting page |

The agent supplies only `url`. The tool fixes the Extract API operation to `crawl`; page limits, depth, and content filters stay in application code.

## Configure the tool

| Constructor option | Default | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `"auto"` | Detect one installed SDK or select an SDK explicitly |
| `default_params` | `None` | Set crawl limits, subdomain scope, and content selectors |
| `mode` | `compact` | Select page fields for JSON output; use `"full"` to retain all JSON fields |
| `response_format` | `markdown` | Return the API's Markdown, or choose `"json"` for structured fields |
| `timeout` | `None` | Set the SDK request timeout in seconds |
| `name` | `"web_crawl"` | Give a configured crawler a distinct tool name |

The tool also accepts `api_key`, `client`, and `include_examples`. See [Common configuration](configuration.html) for authentication and shared options.

## Useful SerpApi parameters

Set crawl scope in `default_params`:

| Parameter | API default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_pages` | `10` | Maximum pages to extract, including the starting page; accepts integers from 1 to 100 |
| `max_depth` | `2` | Maximum link depth from the starting page; accepts integers from 0 to 3; `0` reads only the starting page |
| `include_subdomains` | `False` | Include other subdomains of the same website; otherwise stay on the same host |

Content selectors can keep the agent focused on documentation or article text:

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_crawl

read_docs = web_crawl(
    default_params={
        "max_pages": 5,
        "max_depth": 1,
        "include_tags": "main,article",
        "exclude_tags": "nav,footer",
    },
    name="read_docs",
)
agent_tools = [read_docs]
```

Choose selectors that match the target website. `max_pages` controls fetched pages and cost; these tools do not accept the search tools' `result_limit` option.

## What comes back

The default output is the API's Markdown, grouped by page URL and returned unchanged.

| Configuration | Returned value |
| --- | --- |
| Default, or any Markdown configuration | The API's Markdown unchanged |
| `response_format="json"` | A JSON string with a `pages` list containing `url`, `depth`, `markdown`, and `error` when present |
| `mode="full", response_format="json"` | The complete JSON response, including all page fields and request metadata |

A successful compact JSON crawl with no pages returns `{"pages":[]}`. Individual pages can contain an `error` instead of Markdown; compact JSON preserves those entries alongside successful pages. A top-level API error still raises `SerpApiSearchError`.

If a Google or Bing search URL redirects to its dedicated engine, Markdown preserves that engine's response. Use full JSON to read a redirected engine's structured results; compact JSON raises when the expected `pages` list is unavailable.

## Common mistakes

- Treating a crawl as one search credit regardless of page count. Each successfully extracted page costs a credit.
- Leaving the API's default page limit in place when the agent only needs a few pages.
- Expecting `mode="full"` to increase crawl scope. It changes JSON response detail; `max_pages` and `max_depth` control the crawl.
- Assuming every visited page returns Markdown. Handle per-page errors and pages without extractable content.
- Expecting JavaScript to run. The Extract API reads fetched pages without executing JavaScript.
